lesson.title: Fast Facts for 2s, 5s and 10s

steps.say: You already know how to skip-count by twos, fives and tens, and how to see equal groups. Today we turn that skip-counting into fast facts, so the answer pops into your head instead of you counting every time.

Start with the tens, because they are the friendliest. When you count by tens on a hundred chart, you land on ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, and so on. So six tens is sixty. The trick is: the number you are multiplying by, then a zero on the end. Six becomes sixty.

visual.caption: Counting by tens: every answer just adds a zero

steps.say: Now the fives. Look how they land on five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty-five, thirty. Here is the speedy part: a five fact is always half of the ten fact. Six tens is sixty, so six fives is half of sixty, which is thirty. And every five answer ends in a five or a zero.

visual.caption: Counting by fives: answers end in 5 or 0

steps.say: The twos are just doubles, the same as adding a number to itself. Imagine you have eight toonies in your pocket, and each toonie is two dollars. Eight groups of two is double eight, which is sixteen. So eight times two is sixteen dollars.

Here is a mix-up lots of kids make. Someone is asked seven times five and quickly says seventy. But seventy is the answer to seven times ten. Fives are only half as big as tens, so seven times five must be half of seventy, which is thirty-five. If your five fact feels too big, cut the ten fact in half.

visual.caption: Seven fives stop at 35; seven tens go all the way to 70

steps.say: So remember: twos are doubles, tens add a zero, and fives are half of the tens.

lesson.answer: Twos are doubles, tens add a zero, and fives are half of the tens.

practice.question: Blueberries at the farmers market cost five dollars a basket. You buy six baskets. First find six times ten, then take half of it to get six times five. How many dollars do the six baskets cost?
practice.answer: Six times ten is sixty, and half of sixty is thirty. So six times five equals 30, which means the baskets cost 30 dollars.
